## Purpose

Most group projects that go wrong do so for predictable reasons: no one agreed on who does what, when the team meets, or what happens when someone stops responding. A team contract settles those questions at the start, while everyone still gets along.

Your team will write and sign a contract for the [Team Project](../team-project.qmd). Teams are formed at the project kickoff in class on **October 2**.

## What to Submit

- **One contract per team**, signed by every team member, submitted as a PDF named `Team-Name-Contract.pdf`.
- One team member uploads the PDF to Canvas. Every member is responsible for confirming that it was submitted.

## Expectations

Your contract should address each of the following:

- **Team members and contact information.** Names and GT email addresses.
- **Project topic.** TBD.
- **Roles and tasks.** Who is responsible for what, such as research, slide design, editing, and presentation sections. Everyone should do a fair share of the work.
- **Meetings.** When and where the team will meet, including at least one in-person planning meeting and at least one full rehearsal before presenting.
- **Communication.** The channel the team will use (e.g., GroupMe or Teams) and how quickly members are expected to respond.
- **Internal deadlines.** Dates for drafts and a final version ahead of the **November 6** slide deadline.
- **Backup plan.** How the team will cover for technology failures or a member who is sick on presentation day.
- **Conflict resolution.** What the team will do if a member stops communicating or contributing. The first step is talking with that member; if that does not resolve it, contact the Team Leader or instructor **before** the assignment is due.
- **Signatures** of every team member, with the date.

## Submission Checklist

- Every section above is addressed.
- Every team member has signed and dated the contract.
- The contract is submitted as a single PDF.
